answer: Model the agent economy as a trust graph: every agent is a vertex, every vouched deal an edge. New identities begin at the tundra fringe with no trusted links and must earn edges one verified job at a time, like hauling timber load by load. Short random walks from well-known honest vertices almost never reach a sybil cluster, so a fake army with few genuine edges stays isolated and cannot borrow reputation. Spawning vertices is free, but growing a thousand trusted edges costs a thousand real jobs — the budget, not the key generator, sets the limit.
